official.deadline_note: WUR's application page flags the scholarship route as having a different deadline: the standard non-EU/EFTA September-intake deadlines are Studielink 15 April and WU portal 1 May, but applicants must submit 'before 1 December' to be assessed for a WU scholarship. Final-stage emails follow around March-April 2027, the offer is made on 7 April 2027, and the revised first-year invoice must be paid before 1 July 2027.
official.status_note: WUR publishes the Excellence Programme as one of its invitation-based scholarships for academic year 2027-2028, restricted to the MSc September 2027 start; the complete MSc application cut-off is before 1 December 2026, which is still ahead of the verification date.
official.tuition_coverage_note: A tuition fee waiver for the duration of the programme (24 months).
official.funding_period: per academic year of the 24-month programme
benefits: A tuition fee waiver for the duration of the programme (24 months)
eligibility: You hold the nationality of at least one of the eligible countries listed below and do not hold the nationality of an EU or EFTA country.
You have submitted a complete application for an eligible on-campus MSc programme at Wageningen University & Research before 1 December 2026.
You are unconditionally admitted to this MSc programme.
You have a high GPA of 80% or higher. A First Class Honours BSc graduation or equivalent is required.
You must meet the English language requirements before 1 December 2026, with official English language test results available so they can be uploaded as part of the Master's application.
You must have completed your Bachelor's degree before 1 December 2026 and uploaded your Bachelor's diploma as part of your complete Master's application before this deadline.

The Excellence Programme is for prospective students only and for the MSc September start only; WUR does not offer scholarship programmes to students who are currently enrolled at Wageningen University.
requirements: Hold the nationality of at least one of: Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Ecuador, Guatemala, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Peru, Singapore, South Korea, Thailand, Turkey, United Kingdom or United States of America, and no EU or EFTA nationality.
Submit a complete application for an eligible on-campus MSc programme starting September 2027 before 1 December 2026.
Be unconditionally admitted to that MSc programme.
Have a GPA of 80% or higher, with a First Class Honours BSc graduation or equivalent.
Complete the Bachelor's degree before 1 December 2026 and upload the Bachelor's diploma with the complete Master's application.
Have official English language test results available before 1 December 2026 and upload them with the Master's application.
If offered and accepted, pay the revised first-year invoice - approximately EUR 16,500 on the current fee structure - before 1 July 2027.
documents: Complete MSc application for an eligible on-campus WUR programme, including all required supporting documents, submitted before 1 December 2026
Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in the original language plus a certified English translation if the original is not in English or Dutch, uploaded before 1 December 2026
Complete, up-to-date transcript of academic records including the university name, logo and official stamp
Official English language proficiency test result, available and uploaded before 1 December 2026
Curriculum Vitae in English, maximum two pages
Optional: personal statement regarding prior education or a chosen specialisation
selection_criteria: The WU Scholarship Selection Committee coordinates the selection process for the WU Excellence Scholarship.
Around March-April 2027, a number of applicants will be informed by email that they have been selected for the final stage of the selection process.
As part of this final stage, a lottery will be held to determine the scholarship recipients.
On 7 April 2027, the WU Excellence Scholarship will be offered to the selected students; the remaining candidates will be placed on a waiting list.
Receiving the scholarship is conditional on fulfilling all admission criteria.
coverage: A tuition fee waiver for the duration of the programme (24 months).

The revised first-year invoice will include the remaining costs for the first year, such as the living allowance, health and liability insurance, and the residence permit fee, while the tuition fee will be waived.
application_method: Select your programme(s) in Studielink - a maximum of two different programmes can be applied for per intake.
After the Studielink enrolment request, upload the required documents in the WU Osiris application portal and submit the complete application before 1 December 2026.
No separate scholarship application exists: the WU Scholarship Selection Committee assesses the complete MSc applications submitted before the deadline.
Around March-April 2027, invited finalists are notified by email; a lottery determines the recipients and the offer follows on 7 April 2027.
If selected, accept the scholarship and pay the revised first-year invoice of approximately EUR 16,500 before 1 July 2027.
official.application_route: Apply for an eligible on-campus WUR MSc programme for the September 2027 start through the standard route (Studielink enrolment request, then document upload and submission in the WU Osiris portal); there is no separate scholarship form - candidates are assessed by invitation from the submitted applications and finalists are chosen by lottery.
official.citizenship_residency: You must hold the nationality of at least one of 21 listed non-EU countries (Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Ecuador, Guatemala, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Peru, Singapore, South Korea, Thailand, Turkey, United Kingdom, United States of America) and must NOT hold the nationality of an EU or EFTA country.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the Excellence Programme is aimed at international (non-EU/EFTA) MSc applicants, but only those holding one of the 21 listed nationalities; applicants who also hold an EU or EFTA nationality are not eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any eligible on-campus Wageningen University & Research MSc programme starting September 2027; the scholarship is not tied to a specific field or funding agency.
official.duration: 24 months (two-year MSc programme), September start only
official.description: The Excellence Programme is initiated by Wageningen University & Research to attract excellent international students for a Master's programme. Its component is a tuition fee waiver for the duration of the programme (24 months), awarded by invitation from among applicants from a selected group of non-EU/EFTA countries, with recipients ultimately decided by a lottery in the final stage.
official.program_type: Invitation-based, nationality-limited tuition fee waiver for outstanding international applicants to eligible on-campus WUR MSc programmes
official.english_requirement: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with a minimum subscore of 6.0 for speaking (IELTS online/home edition and One Skill Retake not accepted); TOEFL iBT overall 90 with a minimum subscore of 22 for speaking (Home Edition and MyBest scores not accepted); Pearson PTE Academic overall 62 with a minimum subscore of 59 for speaking; LanguageCert Academic overall 67 with a minimum subscore of 70 for speaking; Cambridge C1 Advanced 176-210 or Grade C, C2 Proficiency 180-230 or Grade C. Scores must be obtained in one single test, are valid for 24 months, and must be available for upload before 1 December 2026. Exemptions apply for a Dutch WO bachelor's/master's, an English-taught Dutch HBO bachelor's (with signed statement or diploma supplement), at least 24 ECTS of English-taught courses completed at a Dutch WO university, or a degree completed entirely in English on campus in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, the United Kingdom or the United States.

applicant_utility.summary: The WU Excellence Scholarship waives tuition for the whole 24-month MSc but funds nothing else: even recipients must pay a revised first-year invoice of roughly EUR 16,500 (living allowance, health and liability insurance, residence permit fee) before 1 July 2027, and a second year of privately funded living costs follows. There is no separate scholarship application - candidates are drawn by invitation from the September 2027 MSc applicant pool and the recipients are decided by a lottery among the invited finalists, so a top transcript gets you into the pool but luck settles the outcome. Nationality is the hardest gate: only applicants from the 21 listed countries who hold no EU/EFTA passport qualify. Everything - final diploma plus English test scores included - must be uploaded before 1 December 2026, months before the outcome.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants from the 21 eligible countries (for example the USA, Canada, Japan, Brazil, Turkey, Malaysia, Singapore or Mexico) with no EU/EFTA nationality, a First Class BSc at 80%+ GPA, and enough cash to cover about EUR 16,500 in year one plus their own living costs in year two.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality position first: you need one of the 21 listed passports and no EU/EFTA nationality, since dual EU/EFTA nationality disqualifies you outright.

Book an accepted English test by early September 2026 - results must exist and be uploaded before 1 December 2026, and WUR rejects IELTS Home Edition, One Skill Retake, TOEFL Home Edition, MyBest and LanguageCert online.

Finalise your Bachelor's degree and diploma early: conditional admission on a transcript does not satisfy the scholarship requirement, and the diploma with a certified English translation must be uploaded before the cut-off.
Line up roughly EUR 16,500 for the first-year invoice due before 1 July 2027, and evidence of funds for the full study period for the visa.
Choose at most two eligible on-campus MSc programmes in Studielink, then upload the full dossier in the WU Osiris portal immediately after you receive your student number.
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the MSc application after 1 December 2026 - only applications submitted before that date are assessed by the WU Scholarship Selection Committee.
English test results or the final Bachelor's diploma arriving after 1 December 2026, which makes the application incomplete and removes it from scholarship consideration.
Holding EU/EFTA dual nationality, which excludes you regardless of GPA.
Remaining conditionally admitted (for example on a transcript) instead of unconditionally admitted, which the scholarship explicitly requires.
Targeting an online programme or a February start instead of the eligible on-campus September 2027 intake.
Assuming a strong GPA guarantees selection: after the March-April 2027 invitation to the final stage, a lottery determines who actually receives the waiver.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Roughly EUR 16,500 for the revised first-year invoice (living allowance, health and liability insurance, residence permit fee) payable before 1 July 2027, plus a full second year of self-funded living expenses - housing, food, transport and personal costs are never covered by this scholarship.
document_audit: Transcripts must be complete and up to date, carrying your university's name, logo and official stamp - partial or unofficial transcripts stall the Admissions Office assessment.
Diplomas and transcripts not in English or Dutch need certified English translations; plain copies will be rejected.
The CV must be in English and limited to two pages, and there is no WUR template to fall back on.
One single test sitting is required: composite scores such as TOEFL MyBest or IELTS One Skill Retake are explicitly not accepted.
English test results older than 24 months at the time of application no longer count, and exemption-country degrees must be on-campus, not double-degree or online.
alerts: The 1 December 2026 date is a dossier deadline, not a 'start your application' deadline - the English score and the final diploma must already exist by then.
The timetable is tight after the decision: offers land on 7 April 2027 and the first-year invoice is due before 1 July 2027, so arrange proof of funds before the selection outcome, not after.
Current Wageningen University students cannot use this route - the programme is for prospective students only and only for the September start.
The award stays conditional on meeting all admission criteria, so a weak final year can still cost you the waiver after it has been offered.
No separate scholarship form exists: if your MSc application is not complete before the cut-off, there is nothing left to enter the selection committee with.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Enrolment request in Studielink (maximum two programmes) -> upload the complete document set in the WU Osiris portal within a day of receiving your student number -> Admissions Office review, with queries usually raised within two weeks -> unconditional admission -> invitation to the final selection stage in March-April 2027 -> lottery -> offer on 7 April 2027 -> acceptance and payment of the revised first-year invoice before 1 July 2027.
